skill.name: markdown-pro
skill.description: Create and improve professional Markdown documentation, including README files, changelogs, contributing guides, tables of contents, and local link checks.
skill.summary: Markdown templates and helper workflows for polished technical documentation.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: All 142 static findings were reviewed against source context. I found no prompt injection, credential exfiltration, hidden network call, or malicious command execution. The alerts are Markdown examples, placeholder URLs and keys, and a helper script that runs git with a safe argument list.

remediation.issue: Placeholder credentials resemble real API keys in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly invalid placeholders and add a note that real secrets must never be committed.

remediation.issue: The helper script runs local git and can write a changelog output file.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should review the repository and output path before running helper commands.

remediation.issue: Badge and example links can load external resources when rendered by Markdown viewers.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to replace example URLs and review external badge sources before publishing.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear project documentation that stays consistent across README files, changelogs, and contribution guides. Markdown Pro provides templates, structure, and helper workflows for polished technical docs.
actual_capabilities: Build structured README files with badges, installation steps, usage examples, API references, and license sections.
Generate Markdown tables of contents from document headings.
Create changelog sections from local git commit history.
Validate local Markdown links and report broken internal paths.
Provide templates for README, changelog, and contributing guide documents.
Format tables, callouts, collapsible sections, images, and highlighted code blocks.
limitations: The helper script does not validate external web links.
Changelog output depends on commit message quality and local git history.
Generated documentation still needs project-specific review for accuracy.
The skill does not publish files, open pull requests, or manage releases.

use_cases.title: Launch Repository Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a complete README for a new repository with install steps, usage examples, badges, and contribution links.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Notes
use_cases.description: Prepare a changelog section from local commit history before publishing a release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Project Guides
use_cases.description: Standardize Markdown patterns across project guides, API references, tables, and screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this project. Include overview, installation, quick start, usage examples, badges, license, and contribution sections. Ask me for missing details.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Markdown file for structure and readability. Fix heading order, add a table of contents, improve lists, and keep the technical meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Release Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a changelog draft from local git history since the latest release tag. Group entries by Added, Changed, Fixed, Security, and Maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this documentation set for marketplace readiness. Identify missing sections, inconsistent Markdown patterns, weak examples, and broken local links.

output_examples.input: A new command line tool has installation notes, usage notes, and no README.
output_examples.output: A complete README outline with a concise overview, prerequisites, installation steps, examples, troubleshooting notes, and license information.

output_examples.input: A repository has commits since version 1.4.0 and needs release notes.
output_examples.output: A changelog draft grouped by change type, with short release bullets and references to related pull requests.

output_examples.input: A documentation folder contains several local links between guides.
output_examples.output: A validation report that lists broken local links, affected files, and suggested link targets.

best_practices: Provide real project details before asking for generated documentation.
Review sample commands and API examples before publishing generated Markdown.
Regenerate tables of contents and changelogs after major document or release changes.
anti_patterns: Do not publish placeholder badges, fake API values, or example URLs without replacing them.
Do not use generated API documentation as proof that the implementation exists.
Do not run helper scripts on untrusted repositories without reviewing the command and output path.

faq.question: Can this skill create a full README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft a structured README with common sections, badges, examples, and links.

faq.question: Can it update existing Markdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reorganize headings, improve lists, add tables, and apply consistent formatting.

faq.question: Does the helper script access the network?
faq.answer: No. The link validator skips external URLs and checks local Markdown links only.

faq.question: Does changelog generation require git?
faq.answer: Yes. Changelog generation uses local git history, so it must run inside a git repository.

faq.question: Can it create contribution guidelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a contribution guide template with setup steps, pull request flow, and review criteria.

faq.question: Should I review generated docs before publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. You should verify commands, links, versions, and API examples before publishing.
